title: ToDoList App — Observability
description: Log-based diagnosis dashboard for the ToDoList training app's 12 injected bugs (see BUGS.md / DESIGN.md §4). Built entirely by reading route source under src/app/api/** — not validated against a live Loki instance. See grafana/DASHBOARDS.md for per-panel confidence notes.

options.content:
**All queries here target the `web` container's stdout/stderr, shipped by Fluent Bit's `tail` input as Docker json-file logs.** Every container in this compose stack (postgres, loki, grafana, fluent-bit, web) shares the same two static Loki labels — `job="docker"` and `pipeline="fluent-bit"` — because Fluent Bit tails **all** container log files and the only per-container label (`filepath`, the tailed file path keyed by container ID) is not known ahead of time. So every query below starts from `{job="docker"}` and narrows down to the Next.js app's lines using `| json` field extraction or line-content regex, exactly as fluent-bit/fluent-bit.conf's own comments recommend ("until the app defines a stable `service` field, use the `filepath` label or the presence of parsed JSON fields").

**These dashboards were hand-written by reading the actual route source (`src/app/api/**`), not by exporting from a running Grafana instance — they have not been executed against real Loki data.** Field/label names may need small adjustments once the stack is actually running. See `grafana/DASHBOARDS.md` for a full per-panel confidence rating and a bug-by-bug map of what is / isn't visible in logs at all.

panels.title: Raw log stream — web container (all output)
Error rate — structured errors (level="error") vs stderr stream
panels.description: Query A: JSON lines the app explicitly logged via console.error(...) with level:"error" (profile update, list create/update, item update/delete, admin create/delete/generate-password/reorder failures). Query B: any line Docker's json-file driver tagged stream="stderr" (a superset — catches console.error output even on routes below that DON'T log level:"error", and would also catch a raw Node/Prisma crash trace). If B is consistently higher than A, that gap is exactly the kind of unlogged failure this app is full of (see BUGS.md #2, #3, #9).

panels.title: Login attempts vs successful logins (auth health proxy)
panels.description: Query A counts every 'Login attempt:' debug line (fires on every well-formed login POST, success or failure — this is also Bug #10, the PII leak). Query B counts login_success events. The gap between A and B is an implicit failed-login rate, which includes wrong passwords (401), bad input (400), AND Bug #1's swallowed broken-DB-connection failures (which return 200 with an error body and log NOTHING else) — this is the main log-based way to notice Bug #1, since its failure path has no dedicated log line of its own.

targets.legendFormat: login attempts (raw, incl. bug #10 PII line)

panels.title: Log volume by event (successful operations)
panels.description: Groups every JSON log line that has a non-empty `event` field by that field's value. Member routes log lowercase snake_case events (login_success, list_created, list_updated, list_deleted, item_updated, item_deleted, profile_updated); admin routes log dotted events (admin.user.created, admin.user.deleted, admin.user.password_generated, admin.todo_list.updated/deleted/reordered, admin.todo_item.updated/deleted). NOTE: todo item CREATION (POST /api/lists/[listId]/items, Bug #2) has NO console.log call on its success path at all — you will never see an 'item_created' event here regardless of whether Bug #2 is present, because that route was never instrumented for success. Its absence from this panel is not itself diagnostic.

panels.title: Error volume by route / message
panels.description: Groups console.error(...) JSON lines (level="error") by `route` and `msg`. Route is present on most member-route errors (e.g. /api/lists, /api/lists/[listId], /api/profile, /api/lists/[listId]/items/[itemId]); some admin-route error logs only include `msg` with no `route` field at all (e.g. admin.users.create failed, admin.users.generatePassword failed) — grouping by both keeps those visible instead of collapsing into one empty-route bucket. This panel will surface Bug #6 (admin duplicate-email create) via msg="admin.users.create failed". It will NOT surface bugs whose catch blocks are empty or don't call console.error at all (Bug #5 list delete, Bug #3's empty catches, Bug #2 and admin item PATCH's raw-stack-trace-to-client paths) — those are invisible here by design; see DASHBOARDS.md.

panels.title: Bug #8 — /api/health is not the source of truth

options.content: `GET /api/health` is hardcoded to always return `{ status: "ok" }` with **no real DB check** (Bug #8, `src/app/api/health/route.ts`). It will report green even while the DB connection is fully broken. **This dashboard's log-derived signals are the real source of truth, not that endpoint.** The panel below is the closest log-based proxy for real DB/auth health: Bug #1's broken-connection login failures are deliberately swallowed with no dedicated log line, so absence of a direct "db_connection_failed" event is expected — look instead at the login-attempts-vs-success gap above, and the best-effort search below for low-level driver/connection error text that may leak into stdout/stderr independent of the app's own (missing) logging for that path.

panels.title: Best-effort: low-level DB/connection error text (Bug #1)
panels.description: BEST-EFFORT / UNVALIDATED: Bug #1 (src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts) points a per-request PrismaClient at port 5433 instead of 5432 and its catch block swallows the error with zero logging — so there is no guaranteed app-level log line for this failure. This query is a heuristic guess at what the underlying pg driver / Prisma engine might still write to stdout/stderr on its own (connection-refused text, the wrong port number, etc.). Treat any hits as a lead, not confirmation — and treat zero hits as inconclusive, not as proof the DB connection is healthy.

panels.title: Bug #10 — PII/secrets leaking into logs (plaintext password demo)
panels.description: HIGH CONFIDENCE: src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts logs `console.log("Login attempt:", body)` on every login POST — note this is NOT JSON.stringify'd, it's a plain console.log with a second argument, so Fluent Bit's json_app parser will fail to parse this specific line as JSON (Reserve_Data On means it still ships to Loki as raw text). It will contain the literal plaintext password field from the request body. This line filter demonstrates the leak directly.

options.content:
A real redaction alert would fire on any container log line matching sensitive-looking field names, not just the one known demo line. Example Grafana-alerting-ready LogQL (adjust field list per app):

```logql
sum(count_over_time(
  {job="docker"} |~ `(?i)("?password(hash)?"?\s*[:=]|"?currentPassword"?\s*:|"?newPassword"?\s*:)`
  [5m]
)) > 0
```

This is a **template, not a validated rule** — in a real system you'd also want to: alert on `passwordHash` specifically (never expected in logs at all, unlike a raw password which at least only appears due to Bug #10), route matches to a redaction/security channel rather than the general error channel, and add this as a proper Grafana alert rule (`alerting/` provisioning) rather than only a dashboard panel.
